AFDREV

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
142 PM PST Fri Nov 20 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Break in the storm action tonight into Saturday with cold 
  temperatures and chances for valley fog, especially in the Sierra.

* Next chance for snow arrives Sunday, followed by another storm
  midweek, bringing periods of difficult travel, especially in 
  the Sierra, during a very busy holiday travel period. 

* If you're looking for travel windows before Thanksgiving, your
  best bet will be Saturday and Monday afternoon through Tuesday
  evening. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

Our current weather system is still producing isolated snow showers, 
including a lake-enhanced band off of Lake Tahoe, impacting 
communities to the east. The upper level low will exit the region
tonight, allowing skies to clear. With plenty of cold air in 
place, clear skies, light winds, and fresh snow, radiational 
cooling will be maximized allowing for overnight lows to plunge 
into the single digits in Sierra Valleys, with a few below zero 
readings in the coldest spots, such as Bridgeport and Bodie. Even
the "warmer" valleys of western Nevada will drop into the teens 
tonight. Freezing fog is also likely (80% chance) in the Martis 
Valley, including Truckee and I-80, along with the Sierra Valley. 
There's a 40% chance for freezing fog formation into the Carson 
Sink in addition to portions of the Carson Valley and the Mono 
Lake Basin. High temperatures will remain about 15 degrees below 
normal Saturday with valley inversions in place.

Our next storm system on Sunday is a fast moving shortwave with 
relatively weak winds, meaning cold air will stay trapped in place 
with snow levels generally at all valley floors, though the 90th 
percentile guidance does raise snow levels as high as 5000 feet by
mid-afternoon Sunday. While the jet dynamics and flow is 
favorable, the storm does not have much moisture to work with and 
has a short residence time over the region. This means that the 
snow totals will be limited, with a general reasonable range (25th
to 75th percentile) based on the ensemble data of 2 to 8 inches 
in the Sierra. This isn't significant compared to the recent 
storm, but is enough to cause difficulties for those traveling 
home Sunday evening.

The best travel window to avoid snowy drives in the mountains 
ahead of Thanksgiving will be Monday afternoon through Tuesday 
evening. The timing spread for the midweek system has it arriving 
anywhere from Tuesday night to early Wednesday morning. This storm
has a decent Pacific moisture tap, but also deep southerly flow. 
This pattern will raise temperatures and snow levels in the area, 
while also not being favorable for spillover east of the Sierra 
crest. Once again, not a major storm, but certainly impactful 
during one of the biggest travel periods of the year. 

Looking ahead past Thanksgiving and into the start of December, 
meteograms and ensembles are fairly noisy -- meaning there are no 
defined dry periods, but also no clear delineation of exact 
timing for subsequent storms. As of now, the Friday following 
Thanksgiving is clear, but around 70% of ensemble members are 
hinting at more Sierra snow sometime in the Sat-Mon timeframe. 
-Dawn

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: VFR conditions prevail through the period with low to 
mid-level clouds. A 10% chance of a few and very brief showers this 
afternoon. This could lead to brief MVFR conditions. Winds will be 
generally light and VRB.

Regional Outlook: Periods of MVFR continue for KTVL/KTRK due to 
either low CIGs or VIS. A few showers from a snow band off Lake 
Tahoe could affect KMEV/KTVL this afternoon keeping MVFR to IFR 
conditions. Chances are around 10-30%. There is a 40% chance for fog 
development for KMEV/KCXP tonight, with an 80% chance for KTRK. 

24-72 Hour Outlook: More snow is possible again starting on Saturday 
night for Sierra sites, and late Sunday morning for western NV. LLWS 
and turbulence starts as soon as Saturday afternoon.

-HC
